value.title: Bug Bounty Attack Surface: GraphQL, JSON APIs & WAF Filter Evasion
value.content: {"id": "intel_bugbounty_attack_surface", "topic": "sqli", "title": "Bug Bounty Attack Surface: GraphQL, JSON APIs & WAF Filter Evasion", "source_url": "https://bugbounty.info/Attack-Surface/Web/Injection/SQLi/", "prerequisites": ["graphql_queries", "waf_evasion", "parameter_pollution"], "signals": ["graphql_variable_injection", "comment_inline_bypass", "case_manipulation", "double_url_encoding", "whitespace_alternatives"], "verification_strategy": "When standard spaces or comments trigger WAF blocks (HTTP 403), substitute alternative whitespace characters (inline comments /**/, tabs %09, line feeds %0A) or test HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP) across duplicate query parameters. In GraphQL endpoints, inject within variables rather than query strings.", "evidence_requirements": ["waf_bypass_status_200", "differential_behavior_with_encoded_probe"], "remediation": "Never rely solely on Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) for security. Implement parameterized queries at the application tier as the primary defense.", "description": "Bug bounty writeups and field research emphasize that modern web targets are protected by WAFs. Identifying SQLi requires understanding WAF normalization quirks: comment insertion (/*test*/), alternate whitespace (%09, %0a, %0d), case alteration (uNiOn SeLeCt), and HPP parameter splitting. GraphQL variables and REST JSON bodies frequently bypass perimeter regex rules."}
